scenes.title: Stable Isotope Preparation Laboratory
scenes.reference_notes: The official facility page distinguishes an 890 sq ft analysis laboratory and a 780 sq ft preparation laboratory. It documents mass spectrometers, cavity-ring-down lasers, glass vacuum preparation lines, balances and a muffle furnace. This compact scene combines selected preparation and loading workstations from those separate spaces; it is not their literal floor plan. Inspected official instructional-video thumbnails show a Picarro water-isotope instrument with an overhead autosampler, chained gas cylinders, and a separate black-topped vacuum preparation bench.
observed_cues: Official facility description: instrument analysis and sample preparation occupy separate rooms.

scenes.title: Planetary Mobility Ground Test Laboratory
scenes.institution: NASA Glenn SLOPE / JPL robotics references
scenes.reference_notes: NASA documentation specifies long soil lanes, a hydraulic tiltbed, rover traction testing and optical motion tracking. The real SLOPE facility is 4368 sq ft; published soil lanes are 11.8 m long. This compact scene recreates a representative soil-test bay and sample-inspection zone using Earth gravity, with a generic six-wheel rover. JPL provides sampling context, not a shared floor plan with Glenn. The inspected official tour preview shows a steep soil-covered tiltbed, a rover, metal guard rails, overhead services and a high-bay interior.
observed_cues: Official SLOPE report: separate high-sinkage and GRC-1 soil lanes and a tiltbed.
Official report: rover mobility, wheel slip, drawbar pull and motion-capture measurement.
Published facility dimensions exceed the compact 8x6 metre scene.
